title: Glossary words are committed as they settle

statements.says: Every skill that writes CONTEXT.md or an ADR commits and pushes the change at the moment it settles, rather than at the end of the session.
The commit subject line starts Glossary: or ADR:, so the log says which kind of change it was.
A skill that pulls a teammate's change to either file reads it and speaks up when it touches ground this session already settled.
What to re-ask after reading a teammate's change is a question for the session that read it.
The domain-modeling skill holds the rule, so the skills that use it inherit it.
Staging is by path, so work in progress elsewhere in the tree is never swept into a glossary commit.
A word pushed for a design later abandoned is removed with one more small commit.

More than one person runs agent work against the repo, and a word settled during a long grill lives only in one session's context, so a teammate can reserve the same word for something else and one design has to be re-grilled.
A push has to pull first, so the check for a teammate's change comes free with it.
The prefix keeps the many small one-file commits readable.
A word nobody uses costs less than a word two designs fight over.
Committing at the end of the session, as to-spec already does, was rejected as the only guard, because the window it leaves open is the whole grill, where the words are chosen.
Reserving words out of band, in a shared file or a tracker issue, was rejected, because a second place to look is a second place to forget and the glossary is already the one place the words live.
